column2: On the authority of Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: “Islam has been built upon five: testifying that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of Allah,
establishing the prayer, giving the zakāh, pilgrimage to the House, and fasting Ramaḍān.” Reported by al-Bukhārī and Muslim.

Buniya (“has been built”): has been founded. ʿAlā khams (“upon five”): upon five supports. Iqām al-ṣalāh (“establishing the prayer”): that is, performing it and keeping to it. Ītāʾ al-zakāh (“giving the zakāh”): giving it to those entitled to it.
Bayt Allāh (“the House of Allah”): the Kaʿbah.
Ramaḍān: the month of Ramaḍān; what is meant is fasting its days with an intention.
Knowing the pillars of Islam and acting upon them.
These five obligations are binding on every legally responsible individual.
Everything else, such as the other outward deeds, serves to complete and perfect them, except what a proof specifically makes obligatory.
It is permissible to say “Ramaḍān” without the word “month”.
The Prophet ﷺ guides us to the fact that Islam is built and founded on five supports without which it is not valid. They are: affirming that Allah the Exalted is One,

and that His Prophet is His Messenger; keeping up the five prayers while fulfilling their conditions, pillars and obligatory parts; giving the zakāh to those entitled to it when it falls due; fasting the month of Ramaḍān with a sincere intention; and performing the obligatory Ḥajj for whoever is able to find a way to it, in provisions, a mount and so on.
Whatever is besides these five serves to complete and adorn them, except what a proof specifically makes obligatory, in which case we are bound to do it.
He who abandons the prayer has lost and failed, / and refused a good return and a good final abode.
If he denies it, it is enough for you that he / has become a disbeliever in your Lord, a doubter.
When the miser hoards wealth, it will / bequeath him grief and leave him a burden of sin.
Give in charity secretly and openly; / do not be miserly, but be generous and giving.
You will find what your hands sent ahead as a shade / when hardships weigh heavily upon people.
